title: Let foreign ships carry cargo between Australian ports
action: Remove the cabotage restrictions in the Coastal Trading Act unless a review shows their benefits to the community outweigh the costs and the goal can only be met by restricting competition.
why: Restricting coastal shipping to Australian-licensed ships raises freight costs between Australian ports, sometimes above the cost of shipping from overseas, which penalises domestic producers.

evidence.source: Competition Policy Review: Final Report (Harper review)
evidence.quote: cabotage restrictions on coastal shipping should be removed, unless it can be demonstrated that the benefits of the restrictions to the community as a whole outweigh the costs, and the objectives of the government policy can only be achieved by restricting competition.
